library_preparation_preflight.summary: micronaut-security's core beans (e.g. SecurityFilter implements io.micronaut.http.filter.HttpServerFilter) reference io.micronaut:micronaut-http types that are not a declared dependency of micronaut-security itself (confirmed via the published Gradle module metadata for 5.3.2, which lists only micronaut-inject, micronaut-serde-api, jakarta.validation-api, micronaut-security-annotations, and micronaut-reactor). Without micronaut-http on the test classpath, even starting an ApplicationContext will fail with NoClassDefFoundError when Micronaut tries to instantiate the SecurityFilter singleton bean. The sibling module io.micronaut.security:micronaut-security-oauth2 (already in this repo) hit the same gap and added testImplementation 'io.micronaut:micronaut-http:5.1.11' as a fix; that pinned version matches the micronaut-core-bom import (5.1.11) used by micronaut-security:5.3.2.

library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: Prefer bean-level tests via io.micronaut.context.ApplicationContext.run(...) (as done in the existing micronaut-security-jwt and micronaut-security-oauth2 tests) rather than standing up a full HTTP server — micronaut-http-server-netty is not needed for meaningful coverage of authentication providers, SecurityRule/SecurityFilter wiring, password encoders, token readers/writers, or session/cookie handlers. If a test exercises JSON serialization of security objects (e.g. login/token responses under io.micronaut.security.endpoints or io.micronaut.security.token.render), watch for whether micronaut-serde-api alone is sufficient at runtime or a serde implementation (e.g. micronaut-serde-jackson) is additionally required — verify via actual test/native-image runs rather than assuming either way.
risks: This analysis is based on static inspection of the published POM/Gradle module metadata and jar bytecode, not an actual Gradle build; if micronaut-http is instead resolved transitively through some other already-generated dependency, the extra testImplementation entry would be redundant (harmless but unnecessary) — local Gradle verification should confirm.

If generated tests end up needing serde/Jackson support for endpoint response bodies, an additional dependency (e.g. micronaut-serde-jackson) may be needed beyond micronaut-http; this was not confirmed as required and is left as guidance to verify during generation rather than asserted as deterministic setup.
